user_query: I need an object detection model to locate people, dogs, and cats in indoor and outdoor photographs. The objects may appear at different scales, under varied lighting, and may be partially occluded by furniture or other people. The model will run locally on a MacBook Air with an Apple M4 chip and 16 GB of unified memory, using Metal acceleration where supported. It should aim for a mAP@0.5:0.95 of approximately 0.40 or higher and recall of at least 0.75 for each class. Processing an image within roughly 500 milliseconds would be desirable.
use_case_description: Locate people, dogs, and cats in images.

available_hardware.details: MacBook Air with Apple M4 (Metal acceleration)

model.description: Efficient single pass detector well suited for real time on Mac with Metal acceleration. YoloV8 provides strong multi scale feature representation, good robustness to occlusion, and solid accuracy with moderate compute. Aligns with the target classes (person, dog, cat) and indoor/outdoor scenarios with varied lighting and partial occlusion.

model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Chosen yolov8 to satisfy the medium latency and reasonable accuracy requirements on a MacBook Air with Apple M4 and Metal acceleration. YoloV8 is designed for efficient inference and good performance across varied object scales, which helps detecting persons, dogs, and cats at different distances and under occlusion. The dataset mix (openimages, coco, LVIS, etc.) supports learning robust features for the three classes in both indoor and outdoor contexts, supporting the target mAP@0.5:0.95 around or above 0.40 and per-class recall of at least 0.75 when trained with appropriate data augmentation and balanced sampling. Latency is expected to be around the target 500 ms per image on target hardware with a typical batch size; actual measured latency should be validated on device. CPU only feasibility is not assumed; Metal acceleration is preferred. If Metal path constraints become prohibitive, a fallback option is SSD300_coco or faster-rcnn_r50_fpn_1x_coco can be used, though with potential reductions in speed or accuracy. Consider 8-bit quantization and minor pruning if memory or latency become restrictive. The stated latency category is Medium and the accuracy target is 0.4 mAP with per-class recall >= 0.75.

dataset_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Selection rationale: We use coco2017_det_train as a single coherent backbone dataset to cover all three target classes (person, dog, cat) in indoor/outdoor photography scenarios. Coco 2017 provides robust, large-scale, consistently annotated detections across these classes, enabling cross-class backbone sharing and stable training on a Mac with Metal acceleration. We target 2,000 images per class (total ~6,000 images across all classes; overlap possible since images may contain multiple classes). Available per-class counts in coco2017_det_train are: person ~64,115; dog ~4,385; cat ~4,114, so 2,000 per class fits comfortably within the respective pools. By keeping to a single backbone family, we maximize domain alignment and annotation consistency, reduce cross-dataset mismatches, and meet the performance/latency constraints (medium latency on Apple Silicon with 16 GB RAM). No other dataset families are mixed to avoid unnecessary complexity and holdout leakage. The final per-class split (training-only pools) will be deterministically split by the trainer, with validation/testing held out from official splits as external benchmarks. The approach satisfies the target ~2,000 positive images per class, maintains a balanced class pool, and stays well within the dataset size constraints (per-class availability) and overall budget.
